UPI MDR Rules 2026, Explained Simply

Last updated 26 September 2026

From 15 October 2026, larger UPI payments to merchants carry a small fee called MDR. Here's exactly who pays, how much, and who is exempt.

Calculate your UPI MDR →

What changed and when

For years UPI ran on a zero-MDR model, meaning neither customers nor merchants paid to use it. The Ministry of Finance issued a Gazette notification on 14 September 2026, and NPCI followed with a circular to banks and payment companies on 15 September 2026. The new MDR framework takes effect on 15 October 2026, giving banks and payment providers a month to update their systems.

The new UPI MDR rates

Type of paymentMDR
Merchant payment of ₹2,000 or lessZero
Merchant payment above ₹2,0000.4%, max ₹300
Essential sectors, above ₹2,000Flat ₹5
Small merchant (≤ ₹1 lakh/month via UPI QR)Zero
Person-to-person transferZero

18% GST applies on the MDR amount itself. See every amount in the UPI MDR chart.

Who pays: merchant, not customer

MDR is a merchant-side fee. It is deducted from the money the merchant receives, so the customer pays the same price as before. Banks and payment providers have been directed to make sure merchants do not add MDR to the customer's bill. Surcharging customers for paying by UPI is not allowed under this framework.

The ₹2,000 threshold

MDR applies only when a single payment is more than ₹2,000. NPCI has said more than 96% of UPI merchant payments are ₹2,000 or less, so most everyday purchases like groceries, tea or auto fares are unaffected.

The ₹300 cap

MDR is 0.4% of the payment, but never more than ₹300 per payment. The cap is reached at ₹75,000. So a ₹75,000 and a ₹2,00,000 payment both carry ₹300 MDR, plus ₹54 GST, for a maximum deduction of ₹354.

Small merchant exemption

Small merchants who receive up to ₹1 lakh a month through UPI QR codes stay at zero MDR, even for individual payments above ₹2,000. If you're a small shop owner below this level, nothing changes for you.

Essential sectors: flat ₹5

Reported essential sectors, namely railways, telecom, insurance, fuel and agricultural inputs, pay a flat ₹5 MDR on payments above ₹2,000 instead of 0.4%. That keeps large payments like insurance premiums or fertiliser purchases cheap to accept.

GST on UPI MDR

18% GST is charged on the MDR fee, not on the payment amount. On a ₹10,000 payment, MDR is ₹40 and GST is ₹7.20. GST-registered merchants can generally claim this GST as input tax credit, which reduces the real cost. The GST rate on MDR has been reported as a possible topic for GST Council review, so it could change.

How UPI compares with cards

Even after this change, UPI stays much cheaper to accept than cards. Credit card MDR typically ranges from 1.5% to 2.5%, and debit card MDR can be up to 0.9%. UPI's 0.4%, capped at ₹300, is lower than both.

What merchants should do now

  • Check your monthly UPI QR total. If it's under ₹1 lakh, you're exempt.
  • Expect settlements to be slightly lower on payments above ₹2,000 from 15 October. Tell your accountant so reconciliation doesn't flag the difference.
  • Keep your GST invoices from the bank or payment provider to claim input tax credit.
  • Don't add a surcharge to customers who pay by UPI.
  • Confirm your exact rate with your bank or payment provider, especially if you're in an essential sector.

Frequently asked questions

Will UPI payments cost customers money from 15 October 2026?

No. The MDR is paid by the merchant, not the customer. Merchants have been told not to pass it on, and UPI apps cannot add a new user fee because of this framework.

Does UPI MDR apply to sending money to friends and family?

No. Person-to-person (P2P) UPI transfers remain free at any amount.

I run a small shop. Will I pay UPI MDR?

If your UPI QR receipts are up to ₹1 lakh a month, you remain exempt. Above that, only individual payments above ₹2,000 attract MDR.

Is the ₹2,000 threshold per payment or per day?

Per payment. A ₹1,800 payment has zero MDR even if you receive many of them in a day.

Can I claim GST paid on UPI MDR as input tax credit?

GST-registered merchants can generally claim GST on MDR as input tax credit. Businesses dealing only in exempt goods or services usually cannot. Check with your accountant.
